In 2026, the national average cost to install a dog fence is **$4,700** . Most homeowners spend between **$2,000** and **$8,000** , with the final price driven by fence type, yard size, and location. Budgeting for extras like gate installation and land clearing can help you avoid surprises along the way.


## Dog Fence Installation Cost Factors: What Affects the Price?


Several key variables determine what you'll pay to install a dog fence, and understanding them upfront helps you build a realistic budget. The type of fence, your yard size, terrain, labor, and added features like gates all play a role in your final cost.

### Aboveground vs. Underground


Dog fences fall into two categories: traditional aboveground fences and underground invisible fences. Traditional fences are visible structures built from materials such as wood, chain-link, vinyl, or aluminum, while invisible fencing uses a buried boundary wire connected to a transmitter that delivers an electric pulse through your dog's collar when they cross the perimeter. Invisible fence installation requires a[local professional invisible fence installer](https://www.angi.com/nearme/invisible-fence/) to dig a trench, lay the wire, and set up the transmitter system.


Angi Tip


Some people believe invisible fences aren’t safe for dogs. If you want to consider an invisible fence, you should talk to your veterinarian about your specific pup. Additionally, some states and counties may not allow this type of fencing to be installed, so always check local ordinances.

### Fence Length and Height


A taller or longer fence increases costs because of the additional materials, labor, and structural requirements involved. Taller fences often need thicker posts, deeper installation depths, concrete footings, and bracing, while longer fences simply require more of everything. Labor averages around **$50** , and materials like concrete run **$8 to $10** **per 80-pound bag** , so these expenses add up quickly as dimensions increase.


### Yard Size


Yard size is one of the most direct cost drivers for dog fence installation, with prices ranging from **$10,200** for a quarter-acre lot to **$19,500** for a full acre. Properties spanning 2 acres should budget around **$30,000** for the project.


### Yard Terrain


Uneven or rocky terrain increases the cost of a dog fence installation because it requires additional labor, equipment, and materials to prepare the site. Land clearing and leveling costs vary widely depending on the scope, ranging from **$20,000 to $100,000 per acre** , while clearing a smaller area comparable to a residential pool runs around **$1,000** .


### Labor


Labor costs for dog fence installation depend on whether you hire a pro or take the DIY route; professional installation runs **$10 to $32.50** **per linear foot** (not including materials), while DIY costs **$1 to $15 per linear foot** . Hiring a professional ensures proper installation and code compliance, while DIY is best suited for experienced homeowners comfortable with the physical demands of the work.


### Additional Features


The cost of additional features, such as decorative elements and gates, varies by location and whether you install them yourself. Gates are available at most home improvement stores for a few hundred dollars, and DIY installation can help keep that expense manageable.


### Behavior Training


Getting a dog to respect an invisible fence boundary requires dedicated training, which some invisible fence installers offer as an add-on service. Expect to pay an average of **$50 per hour** for professional dog training if it’s not bundled into your installation package.


### Location


Where you live has a meaningful impact on dog fence installation costs, since labor rates, material availability, and local terrain all vary by region. ## Dog Fence Material Costs: What Determines the Price?


Dog fence installation averages around **$4,700** , or **$15 to $45 per linear foot** , with your total determined primarily by the material you choose and the length of the fence. Wood falls in the mid-price range and offers curb appeal, though it requires more ongoing maintenance. Vinyl and aluminum cost the most but deliver added privacy, durability, and security.


The[average cost of an invisible fence](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-invisible-fence-cost.htm) is around **$1,325** , or **$2.50 per linear foot** , including the collar, charger, voltage meter, and batteries.

## Why You Should Hire a Fence Installation Pro


Installing a traditional fence can be a big job—you’ll need to dig post holes, level pickets, and install gates. Installing an invisible fence requires even more specific skills, like trenching the fence line, burying wiring, and installing a transmitter. Unless you have fence installation experience, it’s best to hire a[local pet fence installation pro](https://www.angi.com/nearme/pet-fencing/) .


### Here’s why it’s ideal to hire a fence installation pro


Hiring a fence installation pro can save you time and labor—here’s why:


-


Pros have the equipment to efficiently dig holes and install posts.


-


A pro will know all applicable codes and regulations that your fence needs to comply with.


-


Pros have experience navigating the permit process.


-


Invisible fence installation pros know all the steps to install the different parts of the system and can do it quickly and properly.


-


Pros know to take care while digging to avoid utility lines and other hazards.


-


A fence installation pro can prepare the land so the fence is installed correctly and lasts for years to come.


### If you want to DIY dog fence installation


Invisible fence installation should be left to the pros, but there are some tasks you can take on to help with installing a traditional or invisible fence:


-


Prepare the fence line by clearing obstacles


-


Find and mark underground wiring and utility lines


-


Remove and dispose of old fence materials


-


Find out if your fence needs a permit before work begins


-


Paint or stain the fence once installed

## Ways to Save Money on Building a Dog Fence


There are ways to reduce the cost of your dog fence project.


-


**DIY installation:** DIY can save you the labor costs of hiring professionals, but only handle if you are a seasoned DIYer.


-


**Prefabricated panels:** Prefabricated fence panels are quicker to install and may reduce labor costs—you’ll find them at most home improvement stores.


-


**Neighbor cost-sharing:** Your neighbor might appreciate the privacy of a traditional fence—it couldn’t hurt to ask.


-


**Obtain multiple quotes:** Compare offers and ask for references to verify their quality of work—remember, the lowest quote may not be the best installer.


-


**Reuse existing materials:** If replacing an old fence, salvage and reuse any suitable materials for other projects.


Next Steps: Finalize Your Project With a Pro


-


Decide on which type of fence you want and look for a pro who specializes in that kind.


-


Ask the pro if your property is fence-ready or if you need to budget for land prep before installation.


-


If you’re replacing an existing fence, find out if removal and disposal of the old fence is included in the quote.

Frequently Asked Questions


A wire mesh fence is one of the more affordable options for creating a dog enclosure, with prices starting at around $1,300. The materials needed, including the mesh itself and fence posts, are relatively inexpensive compared to other[types of fencing](https://www.angi.com/articles/types-of-fences-pros-cons.htm) . Additionally, if you opt for a DIY installation, you can save on labor costs. This cost-effective option provides durability and security for your dog while staying within a budget. However, it's essential to factor in additional costs such as gates, tools, and potential landscaping adjustments when planning your budget for a welded wire mesh dog fence.


Generally, the height of your dog fence should be 3 times the distance from the ground to your dog’s shoulder. For most small breeds, a 4-foot high fence will be more than enough to keep them from jumping out. Medium-sized breeds like Golden Retrievers, Labradors, and German Shepherds will need at least a 5-6 foot fence to stay contained. Large breeds that are also excellent jumpers, such as Greyhounds, may need a 7-foot high fence.


The decision to add a dog fence to your property depends on several factors. A fence can be a good investment for pet safety, particularly in areas with hazards like busy roads. It helps contain dogs prone to roaming or those with a powerful hunting instinct, It also prevents accidents and neighborly disputes if your pet likes to venture onto their property. Also, by installing a traditional fence, you will also gain privacy. Some local regulations may also require homeowners with dogs to install a fence.
